abstract: This paper introduces a natural combinatorial structure of orthogeodesics on hyperbolic surfaces and presents Ptolemy relations among them. As a primary application, we propose a recursive method for computing the trace (the hyperbolic cosine of the length) of orthogeodesics and establish the existence of surfaces where the trace of each orthogeodesic is an integer. These surfaces and their orthogeodesics are closely related to integral Apollonian circle packings. Notably, we found a new type of root-flipping that transitions between roots in different quadratic equations of a certain type, with Vieta root-flipping as a special case. Finally, we provide a combinatorial proof of Basmajian's identity for hyperbolic surfaces, akin to Bowditch's combinatorial proof of the McShane identity.

abstract: We investigate ortho-integral (OI) hyperbolic surfaces with totally geodesic boundaries, defined by the property that every orthogeodesic (i.e., a geodesic arc meeting the boundary perpendicularly at both endpoints) has an integer cosh-length. We prove that while only finitely many OI surfaces exist for any fixed topology, infinitely many commensurability classes arise as the topology varies. Moreover, we completely classify OI pairs of pants and OI one-holed tori, and show that their doubles are arithmetic surfaces of genus two derived from quaternion algebras over $\mathbb {Q}$ .

abstract: We investigate arcs on a pair of pants and present an algorithm to compute the self‐intersection number of an arc. Additionally, we establish bounds for the self‐intersection number in terms of the word length. We also prove that the spectrum of self‐intersection numbers of 2‐low‐lying arcs covers all natural numbers.

title: Almost all simple lengths are unique up to isometry
abstract:
For every fixed hyperbolic torus with one cusp or one geodesic
boundary, we prove that, among simple curves of length at most $L$,
the number of isometry orbits and the number of distinct lengths
differ by $o(L^2)$. Thus almost every complete length level is a single isometry orbit
of at most six curves, and multiplicity converges in mean to the
generic orbit size. The modular specialization is exactly Chen's
density theorem for Markoff uniqueness. We also prove the full Schmutz--Schaller bound for every punctured
torus having a simple trace that is not an algebraic integer,
including any transcendental trace, and for dense families with
integral traces. More strongly, every rational length class on
these surfaces contains at most two curves. Transcendental twists
give multiplicity one, while symmetric families with geodesic
boundary attain the sharp bounds four and six.
The density proof extends
Chen's method using the stable-norm estimates of Doan-Li-Nguyen.

title: The torus with asymptotically the fewest simple closed geodesics
authors: Phuc Thinh Dang; Trong Toan Dao; Nhat Minh Doan
abstract: We prove that the modular torus uniquely minimizes the area of the stable-norm unit ball among complete finite-area hyperbolic once-punctured tori, resolving the McShane--Rivin area conjecture. It therefore has fewer simple closed geodesics of length at most $L$ than any fixed nonmodular torus for all sufficiently large $L$. We also bound the area increase away from the modular torus and determine its leading growth and first correction term as the systole tends to zero, with error bounds independent of the twist.

title: On the Geometry of the Thurston Metric on Teichmüller Spaces: Geodesics that Disobey an Analogue of Masur’s Criterion

abstract: This paper treats Markov-type solution trees for arbitrary real parameters. A continuous function records the values on each tree; its graph changes from convex to linear to concave as the parameter passes through four. The framework extends counting estimates, lattice-curve descriptions, uniqueness criteria, and geometric identities beyond the classical Markov equation.

An improved asymptotic estimate counts Markov triples by their largest entry, with an error smaller than a constant multiple of the logarithm. The argument combines the correspondence with simple geodesics on the modular punctured torus and detailed geometry of the stable-norm ball. Further error estimates use zero-free regions and a hypothesis on zeros of the zeta function.

The paper establishes Frobenius uniqueness for a density-one subset of Markoff numbers. Equal-length simple geodesics are studied through the stable norm on the modular torus. Boundary estimates lead to equations involving rational linear maps, and a zero-one result for 3-adic dynamics excludes a positive density of nonsymmetric coincidences.
For generalized k-Markov numbers, the paper rules out the proposed reversal of order as the parameter changes. This gives a negative answer to Question 35 of Banaian and Huang.

title: Almost all k-Markov numbers are unique
display_title: Almost all k-Markov numbers are unique
first_online_note: HexagonMath public posting of version 1, distinct from the initial deposit on 8 November 2026.
abstract: Fix a nonnegative integer $k$. Among positive integer solutions of the generalized Markov equation with largest coordinate at most $X$, the proportion determined by that coordinate up to permutation tends to one as $X$ grows. The equation is $$x^2+y^2+z^2+k(xy+xz+yz)=3(k+1)xyz.$$

For closed geodesics arising from subgroups of real quadratic narrow class groups, the paper shows concentration of their homology near the Eisenstein direction. It also considers variation of the modular level and a homological supremum-norm problem, with applications to modular forms and group theory.

Hyperbolic orbifolds attached to real quadratic ideal classes are extended to include modular level structure. The authors establish sparse and small-scale equidistribution results, together with discrepancy estimates. The proof interprets Weyl sums through adelic periods and connects them to Rankin–Selberg L-functions, subconvexity, and homological bounds.

The authors study entropies of subsurfaces inside a hyperbolic surface. They establish an ordering property, finite multiplicities, and a quantitative gap near one. These conclusions follow from bounds for non-filling geodesics and curve counts that depend explicitly on boundary lengths and boundary width.

Residue classes modulo an integer determine closed geodesics on the modular surface. The paper proves equidistribution for geodesics associated with cosets of sufficiently large subgroups as the modulus grows. Their oriented homology classes concentrate near the Eisenstein direction, yielding further group-theoretic applications.

The paper gives a procedure for deciding faithfulness of the three-strand Burau representation after reduction modulo a prime. It proves faithfulness for primes at most thirteen and resolves the stated finite-field form of Salter’s question for every prime.

The modular punctured torus is shown to be the unique maximizer of the stable-norm Mahler product. Polygon enclosures, local Taylor estimates, and certified global comparisons provide the proof and a numerical enclosure for the maximum. Combined with the primal-area minimum theorem of Dang, Dao, and Doan, the result also identifies the maximizer of polar area.

For every fixed boundary length, including a cusp, one-holed tori with three distinct simple geodesics of equal length form a dense but meager set. Such coincidences occur with arbitrarily large common length in each open set. The construction uses twisting, three Farey directions, and a locally nondegenerate map of length ratios.

This thesis constructs a Thurston geodesic that stays in the thick part while approaching a filling, minimal lamination that is not uniquely ergodic. The construction on the sphere with seven punctures uses bounded annular projections and supplies a counterexample to a Thurston-metric analogue of Masur’s criterion.

The thesis studies quantitative density of geodesics and orthogeodesics, the length-dependent terms in the Luo–Tan identity and their counting applications, and a tree structure on orthogeodesics. Applications include counting pairs of pants, recursive dilogarithm formulas, and a combinatorial proof of Basmajian’s identity.

We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=\Gamma(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $\lambda$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $\lambda$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.
